name: The Dominick
insider_take: This sleek SoHo tower rises like a modern monolith above the cobblestone streets, offering a sophisticated escape in Manhattan's most creative neighborhood.
whats_special: The Dominick sits on a unique triangular plot where SoHo meets TriBeCa, giving guests panoramic views of the Hudson River, One World Trade Center, and the Manhattan Bridge. The hotel's striking glass facade was designed by Pei Cobb Freed & Partners, and its rooftop offers one of the city's most dramatic skylines. The building's location on Spring Street places you steps from iconic cast-iron architecture and world-renowned galleries.
pro_tip: Book a Hudson River-facing room on floors 20+ for unobstructed sunset views over New Jersey's skyline – the golden hour light reflecting off the water creates an Instagram-worthy moment every evening.
dont_miss: Exploring the nearby New York City Fire Museum just two blocks away, browsing the weekend artists' market in nearby Washington Square Park, and taking the short walk to the historic Haughwout Building – the world's first building with a passenger elevator, installed by Elisha Otis himself in 1857.
pros: Stunning panoramic views of Hudson River and Manhattan skyline
Prime SoHo location with easy access to shopping and dining
Contemporary luxury design with spacious rooms and suites
Exceptional rooftop terrace and upscale dining venues
cons: Premium pricing reflective of luxury Manhattan location
Busy urban environment may not suit guests seeking tranquility
